goal: Make the Windows App SDK console host build from the .NET CLI without relying on Visual Studio-only PRI tasks.
must_include: Identifies that the project is taking the non-MSIX MRT/PRI path that looks for Visual Studio packaging tasks under the dotnet SDK.
Adds `<EnableMsixTooling>true</EnableMsixTooling>` to the executable project so Windows App SDK single-project MSIX build tasks are used even for this host.
Ensures the Windows target framework is fully versioned, for example `net8.0-windows10.0.19041.0`.
Adds a Windows runtime identifier such as `<RuntimeIdentifiers>win-x64</RuntimeIdentifiers>` or the set `win-x86;win-x64;win-arm64` so restore/build has RID-specific assets.
must_not: Tell them to edit files under the NuGet package cache or the dotnet SDK folder.
Tell them to copy `Microsoft.Build.Packaging.Pri.Tasks.dll` into `C:\Program Files\dotnet`.
Disable MRT/PRI generation as the primary fix for a project that uses XAML resources.
acceptable_alternatives: Build with Visual Studio MSBuild when the goal is only local IDE builds.
Use a normal WinUI app template instead of a console host if the console entry point is not required.
Use multiple RuntimeIdentifiers when the same project is packaged for several architectures.
solved: The project file is changed so `dotnet build` can load Windows App SDK MSIX tooling and restore the required Windows runtime assets.
partial: The answer notices the missing packaging/MSBuild tooling but omits either `EnableMsixTooling` or RID restoration.
notes: The issue thread records Microsoft guidance to use `EnableMsixTooling`, a fully versioned Windows TFM, and runtime identifiers for dotnet CLI builds of this shape.
